messages:
maya: quick update — ran a focused microbench on decode-path kernel selection. comparing FlashAttention-v1, FlashAttention-v2 (fused), and paged-attn under small-batch continuous decode. wanted to share numbers and a weird KV-cache fragmentation artefact i saw.

jordan: nice, what setup? model / seq len / concurrency?

maya: model: llm-13b-compat (gpt-like arch), seq=512 decode tokens=1 steady-state, concurrency=1-4 streams (continuous batching on), GPU=A100-80GB, model quantized q4f16. prefill done once earlier.

samir: paste the raw numbers pls 

maya: paste below (p95 decode latency, tokens/sec measured by our bench harness):

```
kernel            p95_ms   tok/s
FlashAtt-v1       18.6     540
FlashAtt-v2       13.9     720
Paged-attn         21.2     470
Fused-attn        14.5     690
```

maya: TL;DR: FlashAtt-v2 and fused-attn are ~20-35% faster for single-token decode. paged-attn is slower on small-batch decode due to extra host/GPU scatter during page faults.

tess: that's a noticeable gap. did you profile where the extra time is coming from?

maya: yep — sampled GPU traces and cupti timelines. main hotspot for paged-attn was repeated small cudaMemcpyAsync + kernel launches when a KV page miss occurred (even though most keys were in the cache). caused ~3ms jitter per token.

ci-bench-bot: bench run 1851234567 finished. artifacts: https://ci.redwood/bench/1851234567 (flamegraph, timeline, logs) :robot_face:

jordan: given continuous batching, does batching hide the page-copy cost at higher concurrency?

maya: partially. when concurrency bumped to 4, effective tok/s improved for paged-attn (to ~610 tok/s) because the page transfer was amortized across streams, but p95 latency still spiked occasionally (outliers). fused and FA-v2 remained more stable.

samir: did you try turning on the small-batch decode kernel toggle (microbatch path) in runtime?

maya: yes. microbatch decode path (we call it small-decode-optim) helps for <3 streams. numbers with that toggle ON: FlashAtt-v2 p95 12.8ms, fused 13.1ms, paged 17.9ms. so paged improves but still behind.

tess: any memory/regression risk with FA-v2 fused kernels? we saw one earlier where fused kernels regressed for seq>1024.

maya: good point. i ran a quick prefill+decode end-to-end for seq=2048 and saw a small perf cliff for FA-v2 if kv-page-size was set low — likely kernel launch overhead + register pressure. filed a ticket: RTX-ker-334.

samir: can you share the profiler snippet that shows the memcpy spikes?

maya: pasted trimmed trace below:

```
[GPU timeline]
0.000s kernel: flash_attn_forward
0.003s cudaMemcpyAsync (device<-host) 0.9MB
0.006s kernel: paged_kv_scatter
0.009s kernel: decode_step
0.012s cudaMemcpyAsync 0.9MB
0.015s kernel: paged_kv_scatter
```

maya: note the repeating memcpy every token on paged-attn path when page miss flag was set.

jordan: hypothesize: if we batch the page check and only do a single coalesced memcpy per batch, we could close gap. is that feasible in the runtime?

maya: yes, we prototyped coalesced page transfers in the bench harness — it reduced the memcpy overhead by ~60% and brought paged-attn tok/s within 5% of FA-v2 for concurrency=1-2. still had edge cases with fragmented pages.

tess: frag = fragmentation of KV pages across different streams?

maya: exactly. small requests produce scattered inserts, causing later coalescing to be less effective. we can mitigate with a KV page allocator that prefers contiguous allocation for active streams. tradeoff: slightly higher memory compaction cost.

samir: any perf regressions vs main branch? CI flagged a small regression last week in decode p95 after merging default pager heuristics. could be related.

maya: i compared to main at hash 0x7f2a — there's a +9% p95 regression for small-batch decode when pager heuristics enabled. repro script attached in CI artifacts.

ci-bench-bot: linked issue: https://tracker.redwood/RTX-ker-334 and CI job 5921 shows diffs.

jordan: next steps?

maya: propose: 1) revert pager heuristic by default for small-decode-optim path, 2) upstream coalesced page transfer prototype to runtime behind a feature flag, 3) implement a compacting/contiguous page allocator for active streams, 4) add targeted unit bench for fragmentation cases.

tess: +1 on feature-flag approach. run the coalesced transfer under canary and measure p95 regressions.

samir: i'll pick up the allocator work. expect a draft PR by EOD tomorrow.

maya: thanks — i'll push the coalesced transfer PR and update the CI bench to include the fragmentation scenario. will post results here once CI finishes. :white_check_mark:

jordan: awesome, thanks maya. :rocket:
